note: The publishing plan, stated as a plan rather than a promise. A topic enters 'queued' only when someone has decided to write it; it enters 'drafted' only when a file exists with a source for every factual claim. No topic here is a claim about search volume, popularity or ranking potential - those words are banned from this register and checked by tools/verify.mjs. The order is a plan, not a forecast.

cadence.current: One guide every two weeks (suggestion S-05, option A)
cadence.why_this_cadence: A guide at this site's standard needs a manufacturer page read in full, a listing read in full, and at least one conflict or gap written up honestly. That is a day of work, not an hour. A weekly cadence at that standard would produce the thin pages this site exists to avoid.
cadence.measured_trigger_to_change: Two consecutive four-week windows in which published guides average at least 50 outbound clicks a month from the site's own collector. Below that, more guides do not help; better ones do.
cadence.how_topics_are_chosen: From Search Console query data once the property is verified (discovery task D-09), and from the questions readers actually ask before then. Not from intuition, and not from keyword-volume guesses this project cannot measure.

queued.title: Does an air fryer actually save you money on electricity?
queued.why_this_one: It is the first real question a cautious buyer asks once they accept the appliance works. It can be answered with arithmetic the reader can check: a stated wattage, a stated cook time, and a published electricity rate. No manufacturer page states a running cost, so the whole value is in showing the working.
queued.blocked_by: Needs a defensible electricity price source. A US federal average is published, but it is a national number and this site should not present it as the reader's own rate.

queued.title: What '450°F' means on four different appliance labels
queued.why_this_one: Three tracked products make a temperature claim and each means something different: a two-minute finish, a sustained setting, and an ambient sensor ceiling. That is a real finding from reading the makers' pages, and no other page can write it without doing the same reading.

queued.title: The two-minute test that tells you whether your air fryer is lying to you
queued.why_this_one: A reader can run it at home with a thermometer and a slice of bread. It turns a specification page into something usable, and it gives the thermometer and the fryer a reason to be on the same page.

queued.title: Rotisserie, dehydrate, proof: the modes people pay for and never use
queued.why_this_one: Directly supports the multi-function guide without repeating it: this one asks which accessories each mode physically requires, and therefore which modes are really included.
queued.blocked_by: The accessory count on the tracked oven is itself in dispute (FLG-024), so this guide has to present the conflict rather than a number.

queued.title: What to do when the listing and the maker disagree about the model number
queued.why_this_one: This site has a documented case (FLG-026) and a repeatable method for resolving it. It is the honest version of a 'spot a fake' post, and it applies to every appliance on the shelf.

not_doing.why_not: A ranked list requires either testing every unit or reproducing someone else's ranking. This site does neither, and a ranking would force it to hide the trade-offs it currently publishes.
It would require price data from an Amazon feed. The site publishes no prices by policy (S03, FLG-016), and a deals post that cannot show a price is worse than no post.

not_doing.topic: Anything generated in bulk to fill the archive
not_doing.why_not: Amazon's spam policy describes scaled content abuse, and its application review asks for robust original content (S09, S19). Volume is the failure mode here, not the goal.
